## CURRENT THREAD - 2026-07-06 - Community-first RGU discovery story prepared

Owner direction:
- Owner challenged the previous Amara-first customer discovery story and asked
  for a stronger research/peer-review-informed discovery guideline because the
  handbook now points to community as the basis of the infrastructure.
- Owner then pointed to the added foundational white paper and institutional
  handbook and asked whether the discovery meeting should add storylines such
  as Pillar of Hope charity in Aberdeen, Onitsha Main Market, Aberdeen
  resident-to-unknown-member trade, Redeemed Christian Church/local church, and
  UK diaspora community coordination.

What changed:
- Added `docs/GSN_RGU_COMMUNITY_FIRST_CUSTOMER_DISCOVERY_PLAN_2026-07-06.md`.
- The new plan treats the Nigerian Society / real community as the discovery
  object and moves Amara into a secondary member case study.
- It includes a fresh organiser message with July 2026 date options, a
  community-first workshop flow, discovery hypotheses, evidence ranking,
  pass/concern/fail criteria, participant mix, and internal source notes.
- Updated the plan again after reviewing the white paper and handbook extracts:
  added a `What The Added White Paper And Handbook Change` section, a scenario
  library, and a scenario-card test for charity, market, church, diaspora
  association, and resident-to-merchant trade examples.
- The white paper sharpened the internal research frame around behavioural
  continuity, behavioural placement, behavioural capital, and constitutional
  traceability. The plan translates those into participant-safe language:
  community memory, reliable behaviour over time, value already earned, and
  evidence that helps a decision.

Unabated truth:
- The old Amara storyline remains useful as a human case study, but it is no
  longer the best customer discovery spine. A single-person story can make GSN
  look like a personal reputation app, while the handbook and protocols now
  require testing whether communities recognise GSN as trust infrastructure.
- The added storylines should be used as scenario lenses, not all as full
  stories in one session. Showing every example at once would make GSN look
  unfocused and could turn customer discovery into a founder pitch. The safest
  meeting format is one anchor story plus no more than two contrast cards.
- This was docs-only. No app behavior, backend, schema, auth, permissions,
  commit, push, GitHub Actions, or Render deploy changed.

Owner direction:

  appearing blank/not showing during testing.

  - manifest shortcut icons now use `/gsn-app-icon-192-v13.png`.

## CURRENT LOCAL STATE - 2026-07-04 - Dashboard Attention Guide notifications path fixed and browser-verified

Owner direction:
- Owner chose `1`, meaning continue local work and do not push/deploy yet.
- Continuation targeted the remaining unverified Dashboard attention popup path:
  the secondary `Open notifications` action that previously could not be
  browser-verified under the minimal mock.

Truth found:
- The earlier route-recovery fix was not the whole story for this path.
- The Dashboard attention reminder existed in source, but it was rendered with
  `display: "none"`, so the user could not normally open the attention popup.
- After making the reminder visible, real browser hit-testing showed another
  phone-layer issue: the Companion toast sits at z-index `2200` in the same
  top-right area, while the attention reminder/popup were below it.
- After moving the reminder away from the Companion area, the reminder became
  the top hit-test target, but clicking still did not open the popup.
- Root cause of the inert popup: the auto-open suppression effect treated
  `attentionAutoOpenAllowed = false` as a reason to force-close the popup even
  when the user manually tapped the reminder. That made the reminder look
  visible but immediately undo its own open action.

What changed locally:
- `frontend/src/pages/DashboardPage.tsx`
  - made the `dashboard.attention-reminder.open` button visible instead of
    mounted with `display: "none"`.
  - on phone, moved the reminder to `bottom: 86px` above bottom navigation so
    it is not covered by the top-right Companion toast.
  - raised the phone reminder and opened popup to z-index `2300`, above the
    Companion toast layer.
  - added a pointer-up open path alongside click for the floating reminder so
    phone tap handling does not depend only on the synthetic click.
  - changed the auto-open suppression effect so disabled auto-open returns
    without force-closing a popup the user opened manually.
- `frontend/tools/audit-dashboard-actions.mjs`
  - added cages requiring:
    - Dashboard attention signal keeps `notificationsTo` wired to
      `DASHBOARD_TARGETS.WHAT_MATTERS_NOW`;
    - the reminder stays visible, phone-safe, and opens through click plus
      pointer-up;
    - the opened popup sits above Companion on phone;
    - disabled auto-open does not force-close a manually opened popup;
    - the secondary popup CTA stays `Open notifications` and routes through
      `openAttentionTarget()`;
    - the attention engine keeps the secondary notifications CTA contract.

## CURRENT LOCAL STATE - 2026-07-04 - My GSN Identity evidence-status fallback fixed and browser-verified

Owner direction:
- Owner chose `1`, meaning continue local work and do not push yet.
- Continuation targeted the signed-in My GSN Identity hero because the earlier
  owner report said the hero was showing weak placeholders/repetition while
  Trust Passport already had stronger identity evidence.

Truth found:
- Browser verification with mocked strong TrustSlip evidence exposed a real
  fallback-order bug:
  - the old placeholders were gone;
  - the status grid had no horizontal overflow;
  - but the hero could still show `Identity evidence building` and
    `Evidence still building`.
- Cause: `buildTrustPassportViewModel()` supplies a default
  `Identity evidence building` label when no backend identity-status label is
  provided. `MyGMFNAndIPage.tsx` trusted that generated default before checking
  `identityEvidence.score`, so stronger recorded evidence could still read as
  weak/building.

What changed locally:
- `frontend/src/pages/MyGMFNAndIPage.tsx`
  - added `sourceIdentityStatusLabel`, sourced only from actual

## PUBLISHED STATE - 2026-07-04 - Money In / Notifications route recovery tightened

Owner direction:
- Owner reported that the Money In `/app/payment/pool` collapsed/header action
  behavior is unreliable on phone and that opening notifications from the
  attention surface can land on the "Welcome back" sign-in screen.
- Owner authorized downloading the missing Playwright browser binary for real
  browser verification.
- Completed fix was committed, pushed to `main`, and deployed through the
  manual Render workflow.

Truth found:
- "Welcome back" is the Sign In page, not the Welcome guide page.
- `/app/payment/pool` and `/app/notifications` are protected app routes.
  If the local token is missing, stale, or rejected by the API, `RequireAuth`
  sends the user to Sign In recovery.
- The old recovery path depended on React router state when there was no
  stored app-route recovery marker. That state can be lost during mobile
  browser/PWA context changes, so the sign-in page may not know the exact
  protected page the user was trying to open.
- The mobile app shell drawer/tool links were closing their overlay during the
  same click that performs navigation. On fragile mobile click handling, that
  can shift the surface under the finger while the shared mobile tap guard is
  still processing.
- Real browser verification then exposed the deeper phone bug: the closed
  mobile Tools panel was invisible but still letting its child controls receive
  pointer events. Playwright showed the hidden `Close page actions` button
  intercepting taps meant for the visible top `Tools` button.

What changed:
- `frontend/src/components/RequireAuth.tsx`
  - when a protected `/app...` route redirects to Sign In with no explicit
    recovery marker, the redirect now includes `next=<current-app-route>` in
    the URL as well as router state.
  - impact: a stale/missing session that taps Notifications or Money In should
    return to that exact page after sign-in instead of falling back toward the
    generic workspace.
- `frontend/src/layout/AppLayout.tsx`
  - mobile drawer and page-tools links now defer closing the overlay by one
    tick after the link click.
  - impact: the app shell no longer changes the overlay geometry during the
    same click that is being handled as navigation.
  - closed mobile page-tools panel now uses `visibility: hidden` as well as
    `opacity: 0` and `pointerEvents: none`, so hidden child buttons cannot sit
    invisibly on top of the active screen and steal taps.
- `docs/HANDOFF_NOTES.md`
  - recorded the diagnosis, verification, route impact, and publish evidence.

Verification:
- Passed `npm run audit:button-stability` from `frontend`.
- Passed `npm run audit:tap-stability` from `frontend`.
- Passed `npm run audit:payment-instruction-phone-rows` from `frontend`.
- Passed `npm run audit:notifications-button-inventory` from `frontend`.
- Passed `npm run build` from `frontend`.
- Browser verification with project Playwright/Chromium confirmed:
  - unauthenticated direct `/app/notifications` redirects to
    `/login?session=expired&next=%2Fapp%2Fnotifications`.
  - unauthenticated direct `/app/payment/pool` redirects to
    `/login?session=expired&next=%2Fapp%2Fpayment%2Fpool`.
  - mocked signed-in mobile `/app/payment/pool` opens directly.
  - mocked signed-in mobile Money In `Tools` can be clicked, and the `Finance`
    tool lands on `/app/finance`.
  - mocked signed-in mobile Dashboard `Menu` -> `Notifications` lands on
    `/app/notifications`.
- Committed and pushed to `main`:
  `c2705205986d09f659de6cf52690d278f849721d`
  (`fix mobile app route recovery`).

## PUBLISHED STATE - 2026-07-04 - iPhone home-screen icon crop fixed

Owner direction:
- Owner reported that the installed GSN home-screen icon looked correct on
  Android but appeared badly cropped on an iPhone 14/15-style home screen.
- Owner later chose `3`, meaning push and deploy the completed fix.

Truth found:
- The issue was not the app page itself. It was the home-screen icon asset used
  by iOS.
- `frontend/public/gsn-app-icon-192.png` was a broken/cropped PNG even though
  its filename claimed `192x192`; it visibly contained only the top-left icon
  corner and a small shield fragment.
- `frontend/index.html` pointed `apple-touch-icon` at that broken
  `gsn-app-icon-192.png`, so iPhone installs could use the bad asset.
- Android looked better because it could use the manifest/512 path more
  forgivingly.

What changed:
- `frontend/public/gsn-app-icon.svg`
  - adjusted the source icon to use a larger safe margin and a centered
    shield/star emblem.
- `frontend/public/gsn-app-icon-ios-180.png`
  - added a dedicated iPhone touch icon with iOS-safe padding.
- `frontend/public/gsn-app-icon-192.png`
  - regenerated the broken 192 icon so it is a real, uncropped 192x192 PNG.
- `frontend/public/gsn-app-icon-512.png`
  - regenerated the 512 icon from the same safer composition.
- `frontend/index.html`
  - changed `apple-touch-icon` to use `/gsn-app-icon-ios-180.png`.
- `docs/SCREEN_SPECS.md`
  - added the iPhone home-screen icon rule: use a dedicated `180x180` Apple
    touch icon with a quiet navy safe zone, not a cropped or edge-to-edge
    manifest icon.
- `frontend/public/manifest.json` and
  `frontend/public/manifest.webmanifest`
  - added the 180 icon alongside the 192 and 512 app icons.
- `frontend/public/sw.js`
  - bumped the service-worker shell cache from `gsn-pwa-shell-v11` to
    `gsn-pwa-shell-v12`.
  - added `/gsn-app-icon-ios-180.png` to the pre-cached shell assets so
    installed phones can fetch the corrected iPhone icon path.
- `frontend/tools/audit-icon-protocol.mjs`
  - added PNG header dimension checks for 180, 192, and 512 app icons.
  - added a dependency-free PNG decoder and quiet-edge pixel checks so a future
    icon cannot pass merely by having the right dimensions while putting the
    gold border or shield too close to the iOS crop edge.
  - added metadata checks requiring the iPhone touch icon and manifest icon
    entries.
  - added optional built-artifact checks: when `frontend/dist` exists, the
    audit now verifies the built `index.html`, `manifest.json`,
    `manifest.webmanifest`, `sw.js`, and copied 180 PNG still carry the
    iPhone-safe icon contract.

    cache entry.
- `frontend/src/components/GsnInstallPrompt.tsx`

## CURRENT LOCAL STATE - 2026-07-04 - Cover-first PWA entry recovery

Owner direction:
- Owner reported that the app was opening from Welcome instead of Cover.
- Intended behavior clarified: a fresh app/public launch should start at Cover,
  but once the user is actively using the entry flow, Cover may continue into
  Welcome.

Truth found:
- The PWA manifest already points to `/cover?source=pwa`.
- The remaining leak was that `/welcome?entry_from=cover` was trusted forever.
  A restored mobile/PWA URL could therefore reopen Welcome directly after one
  previous Cover-to-Welcome click.

What changed locally:
- `frontend/src/pages/CoverPage.tsx`
  - Cover Continue now writes a session-scoped
    `gmfn_cover_welcome_session=active` marker immediately before opening
    `/welcome?entry_from=cover`.
- `frontend/src/App.tsx`
  - `WelcomeEntryGate` now accepts `/welcome?entry_from=cover` only when that
    active browser-session marker exists.
  - Bare or restored Welcome URLs fall back to Cover and preserve remaining
    query/hash context.
- `frontend/index.html`
  - the pre-React shell redirect now applies the same marker check, so restored
    mobile/PWA Welcome URLs are sent back to Cover before the bundle paints.
- `frontend/tools/audit-entry-auth-contracts.mjs`
  - updated the entry/auth audit cage to enforce this Cover-first/restored
    Welcome recovery contract.

Confirmed verification:
- Passed `npm run audit:entry-flow-polish` from `frontend`.
- Passed `npm run audit:entry-auth` from `frontend`.
- Passed `npm run audit:route-fallthrough` from `frontend`.
- Passed `npm run audit:member-entry-actions` from `frontend`.
- Passed `npm run audit:entry-copy-response` from `frontend`.
- Passed `npm run build` from `frontend`.

Remaining verification:
- If publishing, commit only the files above, push `main`, then verify the
  Render deploy workflow. Do not claim deployment until GitHub/Render confirms
  it.

Risk / devil's advocate:
- This is the strongest browser-side fix without native PWA lifecycle signals.
  Some mobile operating systems may preserve `sessionStorage` across a suspended
  home-screen app. In that case, an app resumed from memory may still show
  Welcome, which matches the owner request for "when in use"; a true cold launch
  should return to Cover.

## CURRENT LOCAL STATE - 2026-07-03 - Marketplace TrustSlip source and Trade Evidence split

Owner direction:
- Owner reported that Marketplace now changed, but still said there was no
  trust value even though Dashboard/Profile/Trust Passport already showed a
  Grade D reading.
- Owner accepted the new Finance Summary logic.
- Owner asked to separate Trade Evidence from the Members/Shops lane before
  later button polish.

Truth found:
- Dashboard reads `getMyTrustSlip()` and uses TrustSlip fields as part of its
  trust reading.
- Marketplace was not reading `getMyTrustSlip()`, so it could miss the same
  Grade D source and fall back to `No trust value yet`.
- Marketplace also had Trade Evidence inside the same visible member/shop
  section, which made two different jobs look like one job.

What changed locally:
- `frontend/src/pages/MarketplacePage.tsx`
  - imports and calls `getMyTrustSlip()` during Marketplace load.
  - stores the returned TrustSlip in local state.
  - passes TrustSlip into Marketplace Trust, Trust evidence, and CCI display
    helpers before falling back to marketplace/community-only data.
  - keeps `No trust value yet` only as the last fallback when there is no
    member, TrustSlip, marketplace, community, or score source at all.
  - adds a separate `Trade Evidence` front card and separate
    `marketplace-trade-evidence` section.
  - changes the old mixed `Trade & Shops` card into `Members & Shops`, which
    now opens only the visible members and public shops directory.
- `frontend/tools/audit-marketplace-front-package.mjs`
  - adds a guard proving Marketplace reads `getMyTrustSlip()` and passes
    TrustSlip into Trust/CCI displays.
  - cages `Members & Shops` and `Trade Evidence` as separate front cards and
    separate sections.
  - forbids `Trade Evidence Record` from being embedded inside the
    Members/Shops lane.
- `frontend/tools/smoke-marketplace-hero.mjs`
  - updates the smoke expectations to include `Members & Shops` and
    `Trade Evidence`.

Confirmed verification:
- Passed `npm run audit:marketplace-front-package` from `frontend`.
- Passed `npm run build` from `frontend`.
- Passed `git diff --check` with only CRLF warnings from Git.

Unabated truth / boundary:
- This is local only. It has not been committed, pushed, or deployed.
- This does not change backend trust calculation. It connects Marketplace to
  the existing TrustSlip source already used by Dashboard.
- If live Render still shows the old trust message, that is expected until the
  owner chooses `3` and the frontend deploy is verified live.

- Owner flagged a live testing fairness problem: a marketplace with 7 members
  hit "quota filled" after only 2 free Spotlights.
- Continue locally; do not push/deploy until owner chooses `3`.

Truth found in code:
- `gmfn_backend/app/api/routes/marketplace.py` was enforcing free Spotlight
  capacity per community with `_max_spotlights_for_clan = floor(member_count *
  0.4)`, minimum 1.
- For 7 members, that allows only 2 active free Spotlights, which matches the
  owner's symptom.
- The May 2026 test-week capacity override is expired today, so it no longer
  bypasses that community-capacity gate.

What changed locally:
- `gmfn_backend/app/api/routes/marketplace.py`
  - added `FREE_SPOTLIGHT_DAILY_LIMIT_PER_AUTHOR = 1`;
  - added UTC-day helpers to count free Spotlight runs by `author_user_id`;
  - removed live per-community capacity skipping from free direct-community
    Spotlight publish;
  - free Spotlight now publishes to all eligible owner-visible communities, but
    the same signed-in global member identity cannot publish a second free
    Spotlight in the same UTC day;
  - paid Spotlight and Network Repost / subscription-credit rules remain
    separate.
- `gmfn_backend/tests/test_marketplace_public_shop.py`
  - replaced the old "skip full community, publish to open community" test with
    a pilot fairness test proving community fullness no longer blocks the first
    free run, while a second same-day free run is blocked for the same author;
  - updated the old test-week override test so the daily identity limit wins.
- `frontend/tools/audit-spotlight-system-feed.mjs`
  - now cages daily global-identity quota instead of per-community free quota
    skipping.
- `docs/FREEZE_POLICY.md`
  - updated the frozen Spotlight contract description to the new daily identity
    quota.

Unabated truth / boundary:
- This uses backend `author_user_id`, which is the reliable identity behind the
  global GSN/GMFN ID.
- It does not require a member to have a fully prepared shop row before the
  quota can be enforced.
- It does not implement the future 55-second rotation/day-cap formula yet; it
  implements the requested pilot rule: one global member identity, one free
  Spotlight per UTC day.
- The future post-pilot model is now documented in
  `docs/CANONICAL_SYSTEM_SKELETON_2026-04-19.md`: paid Subscription Spotlight
  and Network Repost should eventually become appearance-credit / rotation-slot
  products, where each appearance consumes credit and faster rotation consumes
  credits faster. Free Spotlight may later use a daily free-credit allowance,
  but that is deliberately not implemented in this pilot slice.
- The response still returns `skipped_capacity_clan_ids` as an empty legacy
  compatibility field, but the backend no longer fills it through community
  capacity skipping.

Confirmed verification:
- Passed `npm run audit:spotlight-system-feed` from `frontend`.
- Passed `python -m pytest -q` for targeted Spotlight tests:
  `test_shop_spotlight_publish_targets_all_eligible_owner_communities`,
  `test_shop_spotlight_publish_ignores_community_capacity_but_blocks_second_daily_free_run`,
  `test_free_spotlight_daily_identity_limit_blocks_same_author_test_week_override`,
  `test_paid_spotlight_requires_unused_subscription_credit`,
  `test_network_repost_does_not_block_direct_subscription_spotlight`.
- Passed `python -m py_compile gmfn_backend\app\api\routes\marketplace.py`.
- Attempted the full `test_marketplace_public_shop.py` file:
  - first run: 21 passed, 5 setup errors from Windows pytest temp permission
    under `AppData\Local\Temp\pytest-of-chukwuma pc`;
  - rerun with `TMP/TEMP=C:\tmp`: failed in Alembic/SQLite setup with
    `sqlite3.OperationalError: unable to open database file`;
  - these were infrastructure/temp-db setup errors, not Spotlight assertion
    failures.

Deployment state:
- Local only; no commit, push, or Render deploy in this slice.

## CURRENT LOCAL STATE - 2026-07-03 - TrustSlip holder name recovery added

Owner direction:
- Owner chose `1` after asking why a TrustSlip could show
  `Member name not set` even though the join/invite path collected a name.
- Continue locally; do not push until owner chooses `3`.

Confirmed facts:
- Join request creation already saves applicant names into user display names
  when it can.
- Activation already has a recovery path that can rebuild a missing display
  name from `TrustEvent.meta.applicant_profile`.
- Public TrustSlip Verify already sanitizes placeholder holder names.
- The remaining backend gap was the signed-in TrustSlip payload service:
  `get_trust_slip_payload` could still read a stale placeholder directly from
  `users.display_name` and pass it into TrustSlip payload fields.

What changed locally:
- `gmfn_backend/app/services/trust_slips_services.py`
  - added TrustSlip-specific safe holder-name logic;
  - rejects placeholder names such as `Member name not set`, `name not set`,
    `name not shown`, `not set`, `unknown`, and raw public identity codes;
  - recovers a holder display name from recent join evidence
    `TrustEvent.meta.applicant_profile.first_name/surname` when the user row
    has no safe display name;
  - falls back to `GSN holder <GSN ID>` instead of exposing placeholder copy.
- `gmfn_backend/tests/test_trust_slip_display_name_recovery.py`
  - added tests proving TrustSlip payload recovers `Ada Ebony` from join
    evidence and never exposes `Member name not set`.
- `frontend/tools/audit-trust-actions.mjs`
  - added a guard requiring the TrustSlip backend payload to keep safe holder
    recovery and the `GSN holder` fallback.

Unabated truth / remaining boundary:
- This fixes TrustSlip payload presentation and recovery from already-recorded
  join evidence.
- It does not perform a broad historical database repair of existing
  `users.display_name` rows. Account-level repair still belongs in auth/profile
  flows or a dedicated migration/backfill if the owner asks for it.
- If there is no safe display name and no join evidence, GSN still cannot know
  the person's name; it will show `GSN holder <GSN ID>`.

Routes/screens affected:
- Backend `/trust-slips/me` payload path.
- Signed-in TrustSlip and any TrustSlip surface using
  `get_trust_slip_payload`.
- Public verify remains additionally protected by its existing sanitizer.

Confirmed verification:
- Passed `python -m pytest gmfn_backend\tests\test_trust_slip_display_name_recovery.py gmfn_backend\tests\test_auth_profile_update.py::test_activate_membership_recovers_display_name_from_join_evidence`
  with `SECRET_KEY=pytest-trustslip-name-recovery`.
- Passed `npm run audit:trust-actions` from `frontend`.

- Passed `npm run build` from `frontend`.

## CURRENT LOCAL STATE - 2026-07-03 - Profile display name now saves to the account

Owner direction:

- This slice followed the TrustSlip screenshot where the public holder showed
  `Member name not set`, then asked why the member name entered earlier did not
  carry forward.

What changed locally:
- `gmfn_backend/app/api/routes/auth.py`
  - added `PATCH /auth/me/profile`;
  - stores a cleaned `display_name` on the authenticated `User` row;
  - rejects blank names and placeholder names such as `Member name not set`,
    `unknown`, and `not shown`;
  - returns the normal `UserOut` account payload after saving.
- `frontend/src/lib/api.ts`
  - added `updateMyProfile({ display_name })` for the new account-save route.
- `frontend/src/pages/ProfilePage.tsx`
  - changed Profile name saving from local-browser-only storage to account
    storage through `PATCH /auth/me/profile`;
  - keeps localStorage only as a fallback display cache;
  - shows a clear success/error message after saving;
  - makes phone read-only on this form and points phone changes back to the
    verified phone flow.
- `frontend/tools/audit-member-entry-actions.mjs`
  - added guards so Profile cannot silently return to local-only name saving.
- `gmfn_backend/tests/test_auth_profile_update.py`
  - added regression coverage for saving a real display/street name;
  - added coverage rejecting placeholder and non-text display names.

Confirmed facts / unabated truth:
- The old Profile page really was only saving name, phone, and country to
  localStorage. That could never fix backend TrustSlip holder identity.
- This patch fixes the account-save path going forward. It does not magically
  recover old production rows that already have no name unless a saved name
  exists somewhere else or the member updates it.
- Raw phone remains outside the public TrustSlip identity surface. Phone should
  continue through verified-phone steps, not this simple profile form.

Routes/screens affected:
- Authenticated API: `PATCH /auth/me/profile`.
- Authenticated Profile screen.

  name because the public TrustSlip holder resolver can then find it.

## CURRENT LOCAL STATE - 2026-07-02 - Public TrustSlip privacy clamp and stronger watermarks

Owner direction:
- Owner asked to check the public-facing official TrustSlip document for
  leakage of information that should not pass outside GSN, and said the
  watermarks are too faint and insufficient.
- No commit, push, GitHub workflow dispatch, or Render deploy was performed in
  this slice.

What changed locally:
- `gmfn_backend/app/api/routes/trust_slips.py`
  - clamped unauthenticated public TrustSlip visibility to `minimal` or
    `standard`; public links can no longer upgrade themselves to `detailed`
    with `?level=detailed`;
  - rebuilt old detailed snapshots through the public-safe visibility view
    before serving public verification;
  - scrubbed public TrustSlip JSON `merchant_view` so sponsor lists, internal
    contacts, masked email/contact fields, repayment timing, risk flags,
    discipline summaries, raw event/note fields, and bank/contact identifiers
    do not travel in the public verifier payload;
  - removed top-level public JSON fields for masked holder email, repayment
    timing, risk flags, discipline summaries, and human terms;
  - clamped public share-text and QR helper visibility to the same public-safe
    levels;
  - strengthened backend-rendered `/trust-slips/verify/:code/page` and `/lite`
    papers with repeated visible GSN watermark fields through the body.
- `frontend/src/components/TrustPaperMarks.tsx`
  - increased the default recurring trust-paper watermark field opacity.
- `frontend/src/pages/trustSlipVerify/TrustSlipVerifyPublicPaper.tsx`
  - strengthened the TrustSlip public paper GSN brand watermark and recurring
    watermark field.
- Audit/test guards updated:
  - `frontend/tools/audit-trust-actions.mjs`
  - `gmfn_backend/tests/test_community_member_verifications.py`
  - `gmfn_backend/tests/test_institutional_pdf_surfaces.py`

Routes/screens affected:
- Public JSON: `GET /trust-slips/verify/{code}`.
- Public share text: `GET /trust-slips/verify/{code}/share-text`.
- Public QR: `GET /trust-slips/verify/{code}/qr.png`.
- Public HTML/lite papers: `/trust-slips/verify/{code}/page`,
  `/trust-slips/verify/{code}/lite`, and `/trust-slips/verify/{code}/print`.
- React public TrustSlip paper: `/t/:code` and `/t/:code/lite`.

Verification:
- Passed `npm run audit:trust-actions` from `frontend`.
- Passed targeted backend tests:
  `test_public_trustslip_verify_does_not_upgrade_or_leak_private_payload`,
  `test_backend_trustslip_verify_page_links_scoped_member_credential`, and
  `test_public_trust_slip_verify_page_title_and_links_are_institutional`.
- Passed wider backend files:
  `python -m pytest tests/test_community_member_verifications.py tests/test_institutional_pdf_surfaces.py -q`
  from `gmfn_backend` (`60 passed`).
- Passed `npm exec -- tsc -b --pretty false` from `frontend`.
- Passed `npm run build` from `frontend`.

Truth boundary / devil's advocate:
- Confirmed leak: the public verifier could previously honor detailed public
  visibility and could expose masked emails/contact lists through
  `merchant_view`; it also returned top-level masked holder email and repayment
  timing fields. Those are now blocked on the public verifier.
- Confirmed visual weakness: backend public TrustSlip papers had only a faint
  edge watermark; they now carry repeated GSN watermark fields through the body.
- Still not perfect architecture: the signed-in TrustSlip Verify UI still uses
  the public verification endpoint as one data source. The public endpoint is
  now safer, but a later cleanup should move private evidence to a clearly
  authenticated-only endpoint instead of relying on public payload shape.
- Not confirmed visually: no fresh phone/browser screenshot was taken after
  this slice.

  - added a local Money In member-GSN resolver that checks the signed-in user,
    explicit selected-community member fields, and the stored signed-in GSN ID;
  - rejects `GMFN-C-...` values so a Community ID cannot be mistaken for a
    member GSN ID;
  - uses that resolved member GSN ID for the visible `GSN ID` chip, Money In
    identity readiness, route loading, and task storage;
  - stores a resolved member GSN ID back into the normal signed-in GSN ID cache
    when a safe fallback is found;

    yet`, because the problem can be a missing frontend identity handoff rather
    than a truly unissued ID.

  - added a focused audit requiring the Money In fallback resolver and the
    Community-ID rejection guard.

  - added `audit:money-in-identity-fallback`.

Routes/screens affected:
- `/app/money-in` / Money In payment-reference generation.

- Passed `npm --prefix frontend run audit:money-in-identity-fallback`.
- Passed `npm --prefix frontend run audit:payment-instruction-phone-rows`.

- Passed `npm exec -- tsc -b --pretty false` from `frontend`.
- Passed `npm --prefix frontend run audit:gsn-visible-language`.
- `npm --prefix frontend run build` still fails inside the sandbox with
  Vite/esbuild `spawn EPERM`; the same build passed outside the sandbox after

- Passed `git diff --check`.

Truth boundary / devil's advocate:
- Confirmed: this was not only a wording problem. The UI could block Money In
  when `me.gmfn_id` was empty even if the selected community row carried an
  explicit member GSN ID.

  member-like GSN IDs and rejects Community IDs.

  expose a member GSN ID, Money In should remain blocked until activation/sign-in
  is corrected.

## CURRENT LOCAL STATE - 2026-07-02 - Money In GSN ID readiness blocker clarified

Owner direction:
- Owner asked whether the Money In screenshot was only a wording problem after
  seeing `Community or member identity is not ready` while the page showed a
  community and `GSN ID: Awaiting issue`.
- This was not only wording: Money In reference generation correctly depends on
  an issued signed-in member GSN ID, because the generated payment reference
  must be attributable to a member for finance review.
- No commit, push, GitHub workflow dispatch, or Render deploy was performed in
  this slice.

What changed locally:
- `frontend/src/pages/PaymentInstructionsPage.tsx`
  - changed Money In GSN ID resolution to match Marketplace parity:
    `me.gmfn_id` first, then the stored issued GSN ID fallback;
  - changed initial route loading to use the same stored issued GSN ID fallback
    before deciding that Money In cannot load member-specific money data;
  - added `moneyInIdentityBlocker` to name the exact missing prerequisite:
    missing community vs missing issued GSN ID;
  - changed the hero/result state to say `Finish member ID first` when the
    signed-in user has no issued GSN ID;
  - added an inline warning under the `Paying into` identity chips explaining:
    `Your GSN ID is still awaiting issue. Sign in again or finish member
    activation, then return to Money In.`;
  - disabled `Generate reference` and desktop `Refresh` while the member GSN ID
    is missing, instead of letting the page look ready and then fail with a
    vague message;
  - kept the backend rule intact: no fake or memberless Money In reference is
    generated.
- `frontend/tools/audit-finance-actions.mjs`
  - added a positive guard for the new GSN-ID readiness wording and disabled
    Generate state;
  - added a guard that Money In must keep the stored issued GSN ID fallback when
    the live profile response is partial;
  - added a negative guard so the old vague `Community or member identity is
    not ready.` Money In blocker cannot return.

Routes/screens affected:
- `/app/payment/pool` / Money In payment instructions.

Verification:
- Passed `npm --prefix frontend run audit:finance-actions`.
- Passed `npm --prefix frontend run audit:finance-money-movement-lanes`.
- Passed `npm --prefix frontend run audit:finance-front-package`.
- Passed `npm exec -- tsc -b --pretty false` from `frontend`.
- Passed `npm --prefix frontend run audit:protected-button-freeze`.
- Passed `npm --prefix frontend run audit:proof-surfaces`.
- Passed `npm --prefix frontend run audit:gsn-visible-language`.

Truth boundary / devil's advocate:
- Confirmed: this was a real readiness/state problem with vague wording, not
  merely copy polish.
- Confirmed: Money In now recovers the already-issued stored GSN ID if the live
  profile response is partial.
- Confirmed: the fix does not bypass finance identity attribution. If neither
  `/auth/me` nor stored identity has an issued member GSN ID, Money In still
  blocks reference generation.
- Not claimed: an account that truly has no issued GSN ID is fixed here. That
  belongs to member activation/sign-in identity issuance, not the Money In page.
- Suggested sequencing: after publishing or intentionally parking this Money In
  fix, return to the Community Domain cleanup as the next major long-haul lane.

  Community Domain buildout.

  remove repeated explanations, unwanted words, and computer-language labels

## CURRENT LOCAL STATE - 2026-07-01 - Community Session Evidence added to protocol

Owner direction:
- Owner clarified that attendance matters inside communities, but it must be
  truthful, canonical, optional, lightweight, and useful for physical, online,
  hybrid, and offline-first communities.
- Updated protocol docs only. No frontend UX, backend code, schema, auth,
  deployment configuration, commit, push, or Render work.

Protocol update:
- Updated `docs/GSN_TRUST_EVENT_BEHAVIOUR_EVIDENCE_PROTOCOL_2026-06-30.md`
  with a new `Community Session Evidence` section.
- Canonical rule: GSN must not create a separate Attendance Engine; attendance
  is weak Presence Evidence under Community Sessions.
- Community Sessions are time-bound containers under Community Activity Types
  and may generate Presence, Participation, Contribution, and Responsibility
  evidence for the same member.
- Added supported session modes: physical, online, hybrid, and offline-first.
- Added Presence Evidence Methods such as QR, rotating QR, short session code,
  local proximity, coordinator check-in, administrator confirmation, trusted
  member attestation, offline capture with later sync, online attendance signal,
  and partner/venue confirmation.
- Added evidence-strength guidance so weak QR-only presence cannot be presented
  as equal to contribution, responsibility, leadership, impact, or audited
  evidence.
- Added privacy and sensitivity defaults for worship, health, welfare,
  safeguarding, children, immigration, political activity, hardship support, and
  vulnerable-person support.
- Updated `docs/GSN_COMMUNITY_SETTINGS_ENGINE_PROTOCOL_2026-06-30.md` with
  Community Session configuration controls while preserving the rule that
  sessions are not a separate engine.
- Settings now cover optional attendance tracking, session modes, capture
  methods, evidence strength mapping, Trust Passport eligibility, Community
  Verification eligibility, reporting eligibility, repeated-presence caps, and
  low-bandwidth/offline-first support.

Latest unabated truth:
- This is protocol/documentation only. It does not implement QR, Bluetooth,
  offline sync, session records, or Trust Event generation in code yet.
- It intentionally prevents attendance from becoming inflated trust by defining
  attendance as low-strength Presence Evidence unless strengthened by method,
  confirmation, attestation, or audit.
- Still local only. This has not been committed, pushed, or deployed to Render.

  Community Type may seed activity catalogue templates, evidence requirements,

Latest Community Confirmation continuation:
- Verified a decision-status gap in `update_confirmation_decision_status`:
  the service records the requested status and then independently applies
  optional `issue_reported` / `settled` flags. A payload could therefore say
  `status=settled` while sending `settled=false`, or say
  `status=issue_reported` while sending `issue_reported=false`.
- Updated `gmfn_backend/app/api/routes/community_confirmations.py` so
  `CommunityConfirmationDecisionStatusIn` now rejects:
  - `status=settled` unless `settled=true`;
  - `status=issue_reported` unless `issue_reported=true`;
  - `status=cancelled` when combined with `settled=true`.
- Added regression coverage in
  `gmfn_backend/tests/test_community_confirmation_relay.py` proving these
  contradictory status payloads return 422, do not mutate the decision row,
  and do not create a `community_confirmation.decision_status_updated` Trust
  Event. The valid settled status update still works.

Important false-start lesson:
- I initially tested a stricter policy scope/node consistency rule, but the
  full Community Domain suite proved that assumption was wrong.
- Existing behavior intentionally supports:
  - `scope_type: "node"` without a specific `community_node_id`, meaning a
    node-scoped policy template can apply across nodes;
  - node-targeted policies reviewed by domain admins, meaning
    `review_mode: "domain_admin_review"` is not the same thing as domain-only
    policy attachment.
- That attempted constraint was removed before final verification. Do not
  reintroduce it without a product decision.

## CURRENT LOCAL STATE - 2026-06-30 - Community Domain membership requests block duplicate/stale intake, recovery dead ends, and applicant-status review leaks

Owner direction:
- Owner chose `1` after the publish/deploy attempt, so continue long-haul local
  work without another routine push/deploy.

What changed locally:
- Continued the same local Community Domain membership-request hardening slice
  after the owner chose `1` again.
- Hardened the denied-access recovery selector so the frontend no longer
  depends only on backend list order when choosing the applicant's current
  membership request. It now ignores superseded parents, sorts the remaining
  rows by `updated_at`, then `created_at`, then review id, and prefers the
  newest open request before falling back to closed history. This keeps the
  recovery panel pointed at the right child/follow-up request even if a status
  response or client-side merge is reordered later.
- Tightened the self-service membership-access classifier on both backend and
  frontend. A row is no longer treated as an applicant self-service membership
  request only because it is a self-targeted `domain_member.upsert` with
  `previous_status`; it must also carry the exact applicant access shape
  with explicit `role=member` and explicit `status=active`. The classifier no
  longer defaults missing `role` or `status` into the self-service shape. This
  prevents self-targeted role/admin or incomplete governance reviews from
  blocking `/membership-requests`, appearing in `/membership-requests/my`, or
  surfacing in the owner/admin Access Requests panel as if they were ordinary
  access/reactivation requests.
- Added backend regression coverage proving a self-targeted role governance
  review and an incomplete self-targeted governance review with
  `previous_status` are hidden from the applicant status route and do not block
  a real self-service membership request. Updated the Community Domain product
  contract audit to cage the backend helper, frontend filter, and regression
  test.
- Tightened the owner/admin Access Requests ordering after merging pending
  reviewer queue items with approved-but-unapplied action reviews. The
  frontend now sorts self-service access/reactivation requests so `approved`
  rows that are ready to add appear before `pending_review`, then `pending`,
  with newer rows first inside each group. This keeps ready-to-apply membership
  changes visible in the compact first-three panel instead of hiding them
  behind older pending decisions. The product contract audit now cages that
  ordering.
- Corrected stale backend cancellation error copy. Because applicant-owned
  self-service membership requests can now be withdrawn while pending,
  needs-changes, or approved-but-unapplied, the generic
  `community_domain_review_not_cancellable` message no longer says only
  pending reviews can be cancelled. It now truthfully says the review cannot be
  cancelled in its current status. Targeted requester/scoped-admin cancel tests
  and the Community Domain product contract audit cage the neutral wording.
- Tightened the applicant-only membership-request status contract. The backend
  now uses `_membership_request_status_payload(...)` for
  `GET /community-domains/{id}/membership-requests/my`, stripping reviewer-side
  `decision`, `decision_note`, `decided_by_user_id`, `applied_by_user_id`,
  `policy_id`, `policy_key`, `recusal_count`, and `decisions` while preserving
  safe request status, timestamps, self-service request payload,
  `required_approvals`, and `approval_count` so applicants can still understand
  progress without seeing reviewer-private or governance-routing internals.
- Reused the same scoped applicant payload for duplicate membership-request
  errors from `POST /community-domains/{id}/membership-requests`. This closes a
  second leak path where an approved, pending-review, or needs-changes
  applicant request could previously return full reviewer decision details in
  the 409 `community_domain_membership_request_pending` detail.
- Updated the membership-request status boundary copy to state that the route
  does not expose the reviewer queue, reviewer identities, decision notes, or
  decision records.
- Added a backend regression helper asserting applicant membership status
  payloads never include reviewer-private keys, then used it across pending,
  pending-review, rejected, and duplicate-request paths.
- Updated the Community Domain product contract audit to cage the scoped
  applicant payload helper, duplicate-error use, requester-status route use,
  and regression helper.
- Extended the same scoped applicant response to self-service membership
  request revision and cancellation responses. Applicant-created revisions now
  return scoped `previous_action_review` and `action_review` payloads, and
  applicant withdrawal of pending, needs-changes, or approved-but-unapplied
  membership requests returns a scoped `action_review`. Generic active-member
  and owner/admin governance review responses still use the full action-review
  payload.
- Updated cancellation/revision regression coverage so applicant responses hide
  reviewer-private keys while the database still retains cancellation notes,
  requester cancellation identity, and original approval decision history for
  auditability.
- Updated the Community Domain product contract audit to cage scoped
  self-service applicant revision and cancellation responses.
- Closed the remaining applicant response edges in the same privacy boundary:
  `POST /community-domains/{id}/membership-requests` now returns the scoped
  applicant payload on initial request creation, and duplicate self-service
  revision errors now return a scoped `existing_action_review`. This prevents a
  future reviewer-private field from leaking through a less common applicant
  response even if the main status route remains scoped.
- Cleaned a duplicated scoped-payload assertion in the membership-request
  create/duplicate regression.
- Updated the Community Domain product contract audit to cage scoped initial
  membership-request responses and scoped duplicate-revision error responses.
- Tightened denied-access recovery copy after the applicant privacy pass. The
  recovery panel no longer says only "add the missing detail" when a
  membership request needs changes. It now explains that reviewer-private notes
  are not shown, why the owner/admin cannot continue yet, and the first safe
  details the applicant can add: member title, invite reference, department,
  class, or relationship proof. Cancelled/rejected child revisions also now
  explain that the applicant must continue from the revision rather than start
  over.
- Updated the recovery form placeholder/helper text and the Community Domain
  product contract audit to cage that applicant-safe guidance.
- Closed an owner/admin visibility gap in the lazy Access Requests panel. The
  panel still keeps the first three self-service access/reactivation requests
  visible by default for compactness, but it no longer silently hides the
  fourth and later actionable requests. When more than three requests exist,
  admins now get a `Show N more requests` / `Show first 3 requests` toggle.
  This is route-local UI only; it does not change reviewer authority,
  membership application rules, backend routes, auth, schemas, or deployment.
- Updated the Community Domain product contract audit to cage that expandable
  access-request queue behavior so the panel cannot regress into silently
  truncating the actionable queue.
- Added compact approval-progress copy to each access-request card when the
  backend says multiple approvals are required or any approval is already
  recorded. The panel now says, for example, `1 of 2 approvals recorded. 1 more
  needed before this can be added.` or `Approvals complete: 2 of 2 recorded.`
  This makes the `Approve, add if ready` action explain why it may only record
  the current reviewer decision under multi-approval policy.
- Updated the Community Domain product contract audit to cage approval progress
  on the lazy access-request panel.
- Added matching applicant-facing approval progress to the denied-access
  recovery panel. When the requester is waiting on a self-service access review
  that carries approval counts, their recovery card now includes how many
  approvals are recorded and how many remain before owner/admin apply can
  happen. This is display-only and does not expose reviewer identities or
  private review payloads.
- Updated the Community Domain product contract audit to cage applicant-side
  approval progress in denied-access recovery.
- Tightened backend requester-status regression coverage so
  `GET /community-domains/{id}/membership-requests/my` is proven to carry
  `required_approvals` and `approval_count` for a two-reviewer self-service
  membership request. The test now asserts the applicant sees `0 of 2` on the
  initial pending request and `1 of 2` after the first approval while the review
  remains `pending_review`.
- Updated the Community Domain product contract audit to cage that applicant
  status approval-progress payload contract.
- Fixed the owner/admin `Approve + add member` access-request path for
  multi-approval policies. The frontend now checks the decision response before
  calling apply; if the review is still `pending_review` because another
  approval is required, it refreshes the queue and shows that another approval
  is needed instead of making a premature apply call that the backend correctly
  rejects.
- Tightened that post-click feedback so it uses the backend decision response
  counts. If an admin clicks `Approve, add if ready` and the review still needs
  more approvals, the dashboard now says the exact remaining approval count
  when `approval_count` and `required_approvals` are available, instead of

- Updated the Community Domain product contract audit to cage that
  decision-before-apply guard and the count-aware remaining-approval message.
- Made the matching Access Requests button label honest for multi-approval
  policies. The combined action now says `Approve, add if ready`, with a

- Updated the Community Domain product contract audit to cage that truthful
  button copy.
- Tightened the Governance review pulse so it no longer collapses the current
  admin's scoped reviewer-queue pressure and the domain's institutional
  open-review pressure into one ambiguous signal. Admins now see the personal
  `Needs review` count from their scoped reviewer queue plus an `Institution
  open` count from the dashboard's `counts.open_reviews`; if the domain still

- Corrected the follow-up edge in that Governance pulse: the institutional
  open-review badge is admin-only, so non-admin members no longer see a false
  `Institution open: 0` beside their broader review-pressure summary.
- Updated the Community Domain product contract audit to cage that distinction
  between scoped reviewer work and institutional review pressure.
- Closed the same `needs_changes` queue-label drift in node-local read-only
  summaries. Node operating summaries, node status-impact snapshots, and member
  placement summaries now count only `pending`, `pending_review`, and

  remain recorded, but they no longer drive `review_local_queue` or
  `review_member_queue` guidance because that status means requester follow-up,
  not a reviewer decision waiting in the local queue.
- Added backend regression coverage proving a node/member `needs_changes`
  review remains in the database while node operating summary, node
  status-impact, and member placement summary all report clear local review
  queue pressure.
- Updated the Community Domain product contract audit to cage the node-local
  `needs_changes` exclusion in backend helpers and tests.
- Closed the follow-up approved-work route mismatch in those same node/member
  summaries. Approved-but-unapplied local action reviews still count as open
  apply work, but the summaries no longer point users at the pending-only
  `reviewer-queue`. Node operating summary now routes local open/apply work to
  `/action-reviews?community_node_id=...&include_descendants=true`, and member

  `/action-reviews?user_id=...`.
- Added an admin-only `user_id` filter to `GET
  /community-domains/{id}/action-reviews` so member placement summary route
  hints land on a real member-specific action-review list. The filter matches
  `subject_user_id` plus domain/member/node-member target rows, stays inside
  the existing domain/node admin scope, and does not grant reviewer authority.
- Added regression coverage proving an approved-but-unapplied node/member
  review appears through the action-review list route hints while the
  pending-only reviewer queue stays empty.
- Closed an older node-scoped reviewer-queue route-hint mismatch. The backend
  reviewer queue now accepts `community_node_id` and `include_descendants`,
  filters candidate pending reviews by the requested node scope before
  reviewer authorization, and returns the scoped `community_node_id` /
  `community_node_ids` metadata. This makes existing
  `/action-reviews/reviewer-queue?community_node_id=...` links truthful instead
  of decorative.
- Updated the shared frontend API helper so `listCommunityDomainActionReviews`
  can send `user_id`, and `getCommunityDomainReviewerQueue` can send
  `community_node_id` and `include_descendants`. This keeps the client contract
  aligned with the new backend filters without changing dashboard behavior.
- Added backend regression coverage proving an unfiltered reviewer queue shows
  two decidable node reviews while node-filtered queues return only the
  requested node's pending review.
- Tightened the frontend owner/admin access-request classifier to mirror the
  backend self-service membership review guard. The Access Requests panel now
  requires `requested_by_user_id`, `subject_user_id`, `target_id`, and
  `payload.user_id` to all identify the same requester, in addition to the
  `domain_member.upsert`, `domain_member`, and `previous_status` checks. This
  prevents a generic membership governance review that happens to carry
  `previous_status` from being mislabeled as a self-service access/reactivation
  request.
- Updated the Community Domain product contract audit to cage that stricter
  frontend identity match.
- Closed a backend lineage edge after applying a child membership revision.
  The duplicate guard previously still treated the old `needs_changes` parent
  as an open blocker, so if the child revision had been applied and the member
  was later set inactive, a legitimate reactivation request could be rejected
  with `community_domain_membership_request_pending`.
- Added `_self_service_membership_review_ids_with_applied_descendant(...)` and
  changed `POST /community-domains/{id}/membership-requests` so only open
  self-service request rows without an applied descendant block fresh intake.
  Cancelled child revisions still keep the continuation path locked, while an
  applied descendant releases its superseded parent.
- Added backend regression coverage proving an applied child revision no
  longer blocks a later inactive-member reactivation request, and updated the
  Community Domain product contract audit to cage that lineage rule.
- Closed the matching denied-access UI loop. The recovery panel previously
  treated an `applied` historical access review as a reason to make the access
  button retry the dashboard. After a member is later inactive, that traps the
  user even though the backend now allows a fresh reactivation request.
- Updated `DashboardRecoveryPanel` so an applied historical request explains
  both options: retry the dashboard, or send a fresh access request if current
  membership is no longer active. The primary retry button remains available,
  but the access button now calls the real request route instead of retrying.
- Updated the Community Domain product contract audit to prevent applied
  historical reviews in the denied-access recovery panel from being wired back
  to dashboard retry instead of reactivation intake.
- Added a requester-status regression assertion to the applied-child
  reactivation test. After a later inactive-member reactivation request is
  created, `GET /community-domains/{id}/membership-requests/my` must list the
  new pending reactivation first while still retaining the older applied review
  in history. This cages the ordering the denied-access recovery panel depends

- Updated the Community Domain product contract audit to cage that requester
  status ordering. Confirmed, but did not change, that generic action-review

- Closed an approved-but-unapplied applicant withdrawal dead end. Approved
  self-service membership requests still blocked duplicate intake but could not
  be withdrawn before an owner/admin applied them, which trapped the original
  requester if they no longer wanted the membership added.
- Updated `POST /community-domains/{id}/action-reviews/{review_id}/cancel` so
  the original applicant can cancel their own self-service
  `domain_member.upsert` membership request while it is `approved` but
  unapplied. Generic action-review cancellation remains pending-only, and

- Updated `DashboardRecoveryPanel` so approved-but-unapplied access requests
  explain that membership still needs owner/admin apply, while allowing the
  applicant to withdraw before apply. The request button now says
  `Withdraw request` for approved self-service access requests instead of a
  locked `Approved, waiting to add` state.
- Added backend regression coverage proving approved-but-unapplied applicant
  withdrawal releases duplicate intake and creates no membership, and updated
  the Community Domain product contract audit to cage backend + frontend
  behavior.
- Corrected the cancel response boundary from "before approval/application" to
  "before application" so approved-but-unapplied withdrawal is described
  truthfully. The approved-withdrawal regression now also asserts the original
  approval decision record remains in review history after row-level status is
  changed to `cancelled`.
- Tightened the same regression to prove owner/admin apply cannot happen after
  the applicant withdraws the approved-but-unapplied request. Applying the
  cancelled review now remains caged by the existing
  `community_domain_review_not_approved` guard.
- Tightened the owner/admin side of the same revision lineage. The reviewer
  queue endpoint now uses `REVIEWER_QUEUE_PENDING_STATUSES`, the same
  pending-only status constant used by dashboard/readiness/operating-map
  reviewer guidance, instead of carrying its own hard-coded pending list.
- Added backend regression coverage proving a `needs_changes` self-service
  membership-request parent does not appear as reviewer work, while a later
  pending child revision does appear in the owner/admin reviewer queue as the
  review that can actually be decided.
- Updated the Community Domain product contract audit to cage the reviewer
  queue's pending-only constant use and the parent-hidden/child-visible
  membership revision queue behavior.
- Closed a follow-up lineage dead end in denied-access recovery. Once a
  `needs_changes` membership request has a child revision, the parent review is
  no longer the row the applicant should continue from. The backend correctly
  rejects a second parent revision as a fork, but the frontend selector could
  still prefer the older open parent over a newer cancelled/rejected child
  revision.
- Updated `latestRelevantMembershipRequest(...)` to ignore superseded parent
  rows whenever a child revision exists, then choose the current leaf row for
  the recovery panel. This keeps the UI pointed at the review the backend
  expects the applicant to continue.
- Updated `DashboardRecoveryPanel` so cancelled/rejected child revisions with a
  `parent_review_id` show the inline update form and `Send update` action
  instead of nudging a fresh request that the duplicate guard will reject.
  Root cancelled/rejected requests still fall back to the normal request-again

- Added backend regression coverage proving that after a child membership
  revision is cancelled, a fresh duplicate membership request remains blocked
  but the applicant can revise the cancelled child without forking the
  `needs_changes` parent.
- Updated the Community Domain product contract audit to cage superseded-parent
  filtering, continuation child UI behavior, and the cancelled-child backend
  lineage regression.
- Closed the frontend half of the applicant revision path. The backend already
  allowed a non-member applicant to revise their own self-service Community
  Domain membership request after owner/admin `needs_changes`, but the denied
  dashboard recovery panel still only made withdrawal obvious.
- Updated `CommunityDomainDashboardPage` to import and call
  `reviseCommunityDomainActionReview` from the denied-access recovery path,
  refresh the signed-in applicant's own membership-request status, and keep the
  success message explicit that owner/admin approval and apply are still
  required before membership changes.
- Updated the lazy `DashboardRecoveryPanel` so a `needs_changes` request shows
  a compact inline update form for a member title/proof label and a short
  applicant note, plus a real `Send update` action. The existing withdraw path
  remains available for the same request.
- Updated the Community Domain product contract audit to cage the applicant
  revision UI, parent route handler, API helper use, and the no-instant-
  membership copy boundary.
- Tightened denied-access recovery request selection. The dashboard previously
  handed `ownMembershipRequests[0]` to the recovery panel, so a newer closed
  historical row could hide an older still-open self-service membership request.
  That could make the panel look requestable while the backend still correctly
  blocked duplicate intake.
- Added route-local `latestRelevantMembershipRequest(...)` so the recovery
  panel prefers the latest open applicant request (`pending`, `pending_review`,
  `needs_changes`, or `approved`) before falling back to the newest closed
  history row.
- Updated the Community Domain product contract audit to cage this open-request
  priority so future recovery-panel edits cannot regress into newest-row-wins
  behavior.
- Closed the frontend half of the applicant-withdrawal path. The backend could
  already let non-member applicants cancel their own pending or needs-changes
  self-service Community Domain membership request, but the dashboard recovery
  panel still only showed a generic request-access button. That meant the user
  could see the blocker without a visible way to release it.
- Updated `CommunityDomainDashboardPage` to import and call
  `cancelCommunityDomainActionReview` from the denied-access recovery path, then
  refresh the signed-in applicant's own membership-request status and show a
  plain success message after withdrawal.
- Updated the lazy `DashboardRecoveryPanel` so pending, pending-review, and
  needs-changes access requests switch the request button to `Withdraw request`.
  Approved requests remain locked because backend cancellation does not allow
  approved-but-unapplied withdrawal, applied requests retry the dashboard, and
  rejected/cancelled requests can still request again.
- Updated the Community Domain product contract audit to cage the frontend
  applicant-withdrawal recovery path and the panel's needs-changes copy.
- Found a second classification leak in
  `POST /community-domains/{id}/membership-requests`: the duplicate guard had
  already learned to block open membership requests, but it still treated any
  open self-targeted `domain_member.upsert` review as the applicant's existing
  self-service request. That could incorrectly block a legitimate applicant,
  and because the error detail returns the blocking `action_review`, it could
  expose a generic owner/admin governance row back to the requester.
- Tightened the duplicate guard so it first fetches candidate self-targeted
  `domain_member.upsert` rows, then only treats a row as an existing membership
  request if `_is_self_service_domain_membership_review_for_user(...)`
  confirms the review is the applicant's own self-service membership request
  carrying the `previous_status` snapshot.
- Added regression coverage proving a generic self-targeted owner/admin
  `domain_member.upsert` review does not block the applicant from creating a
  real self-service membership request, and that the later duplicate error
  points at the self-service request instead of leaking the generic review.
- Updated the Community Domain product contract audit to cage the stricter
  self-service-only duplicate guard and the generic-review non-leak regression.
- Tightened the requester status endpoint:
  `GET /community-domains/{id}/membership-requests/my` now returns only true
  self-service membership access/reactivation requests carrying the
  `previous_status` snapshot. A generic self-targeted `domain_member.upsert`
  governance review no longer appears as an applicant membership request just
  because the requester, subject, and target happen to be the same user.
- Added regression coverage by inserting a generic self-targeted
  `domain_member.upsert` review beside a real self-service membership request;
  the endpoint returns only the self-service request and leaves the generic
  review hidden and unchanged.
- Updated the Community Domain product contract audit to cage the
  requester-only and self-service-only status route.
- Found a second withdrawal dead end: after an applicant's self-service
  membership request was marked `needs_changes`, the request still counted as
  open and blocked duplicate intake, but the cancel endpoint only allowed
  `pending`/`pending_review` cancellation. That meant an applicant could revise
  or remain blocked, but could not withdraw and restart.
- Narrowed cancellation status handling so only the original self-service
  membership requester can cancel their own `needs_changes` access request.
  Generic action reviews still use the existing pending-only cancellation rule.
- Added regression coverage proving a non-member applicant can cancel their own
  `needs_changes` membership request, the cancelled review releases the
  duplicate guard for a fresh request, and cancellation does not create
  membership.
- Updated the Community Domain product contract audit to cage both pending and
  needs-changes applicant withdrawal.
- Found a withdrawal dead end: a non-member applicant could create a
  self-service Community Domain membership request, but
  `POST /community-domains/{id}/action-reviews/{review_id}/cancel` required
  active domain membership before allowing the original requester to cancel.
  That meant an applicant could be blocked from withdrawing their own pending
  request while also being blocked from submitting a replacement request.
- Moved the cancel endpoint through the same narrow self-service membership
  review recognition used by revision:
  - applicants can cancel only their own self-service `domain_member.upsert`
    membership request;
  - generic action-review cancellation remains member/admin-scoped;
  - requester/admin cancel authorization and pending-only cancellation status
    rules remain unchanged after that narrow gate.
- Added regression coverage proving a non-member applicant can withdraw their
  own pending membership request, that the cancelled request releases the
  duplicate guard for a fresh request, and that cancellation does not create
  membership.
- Updated the Community Domain product contract audit to cage applicant
  withdrawal while preserving generic cancel scoping.
- Found a follow-on revision integrity gap: after an applicant's self-service
  membership request was marked `needs_changes`, an owner/admin could directly
  activate that applicant outside the review. The applicant revision endpoint
  could then create a new pending child review from the now-stale original
  snapshot even though membership was already active. Apply would later reject
  the stale review, but the queue could still be polluted with a resolved access
  request.
- Added a current-membership check to self-service membership request revision
  normalization:
  - if the applicant is already active, the revision returns
    `community_domain_member_already_active`;
  - if the applicant's current membership status no longer matches the
    review's `previous_status` snapshot, the revision returns
    `community_domain_member_review_stale`;
  - no child review is created in either case.
- Added regression coverage proving a non-member applicant cannot revise a
  needs-changes request after direct activation and that the original review
  remains the only action-review row.
- Updated the Community Domain product contract audit to cage stale/already
  active membership snapshot rejection during self-service request revision.
- Found a second backend lifecycle gap: once a self-service non-member
  membership request was marked `needs_changes`, the duplicate guard correctly
  blocked a second request, but the generic revision endpoint required active
  Community Domain membership before checking requester identity. That trapped
  non-member applicants between "revise your request" and "only active members
  can revise."
- Moved `POST /community-domains/{id}/action-reviews/{review_id}/revision`
  through a narrow exception for self-service membership request revisions:
  - the row must be a `domain_member.upsert` review;
  - it must target `domain_member`;
  - `requested_by_user_id`, `subject_user_id`, `target_id`, and payload
    `user_id` must all be the current requester;
  - the review payload must include the self-service `previous_status` snapshot.
- Kept generic action-review revisions member/admin-scoped. The exception only
  applies to the applicant's own self-service membership access/reactivation
  review.
- Normalized self-service membership revision payloads so applicants can update
  request context such as title, but cannot revise the request into another
  person's membership, change the requested role, change the requested status,
  or rewrite the reviewed previous membership status.
- Added regression coverage proving a non-member applicant whose request needs
  changes:
  - cannot submit a duplicate membership request instead;
  - cannot revise the request to target another user;
  - can revise their own request into a new pending review with the same
    self-service scope and previous-status snapshot.
- Updated the Community Domain product contract audit to cage the
  self-service membership revision exception and the abuse-prevention test.
- Corrected the top handoff entry to reflect the real publish/deploy status for
  commit `1e396bdb85d5531dfbbef81722b136668b29e2ef`:
  - frontend Render deploy hook was accepted with deploy id `dep-d91tijnlk1mc73abqvl0`;
  - GitHub Actions backend deploy failed because GitHub secret `RENDER_API_KEY`
    is missing, but the owner later confirmed the Render backend dashboard shows
    `gmfn-api` live at the same `1e396bd` commit, and live
    `https://gmfn-api.onrender.com/health` returned
    `{"ok":true,"dev_mode":false}`.
- Continued Community Domain onboarding/membership-request hardening.
- Found a backend integrity gap in `POST /community-domains/{id}/membership-requests`:
  - duplicate self-service membership requests were blocked only while a prior
    request was `pending` or `pending_review`;
  - an `approved` but not yet applied request was still an open governance
    change, but the requester could submit a duplicate before an admin applied
    the approved review.
- Added route-local `MEMBERSHIP_REQUEST_OPEN_STATUSES` covering:
  - `pending`;
  - `pending_review`;
  - `needs_changes`;
  - `approved`.
- The duplicate guard now blocks new membership requests while any existing
  self-request for the same domain/user is still open in those statuses.
- Kept the existing error code
  `community_domain_membership_request_pending` for frontend compatibility, but
  changed the backend message to say "open Community Domain membership request"
  instead of only "pending".
- Updated the dashboard recovery copy for that error to say the user already has
  an open access request that must be resolved and applied before membership
  changes.
- Added regression coverage proving an approved-but-unapplied membership request
  still blocks a duplicate request before apply.
- Added `previous_status` to self-service membership-request review payloads so
  apply can compare the reviewed prior membership state with the current state:
  - new applicants snapshot `previous_status: "none"`;
  - inactive existing members snapshot their actual status instead of being
    treated as never having existed.
- Added a stale-apply guard for `domain_member.upsert` reviews that explicitly
  carry `previous_status`: if the current membership status no longer matches
  the reviewed previous status, the backend returns
  `community_domain_member_review_stale` and leaves the review approved but
  unapplied instead of overwriting newer membership state. Generic
  `domain_member.upsert` reviews without a previous-status snapshot are not
  stale-checked by this guard.
- Added regression coverage proving an approved self-service membership request
  cannot overwrite a direct active membership created before apply.
- Added regression coverage proving an inactive domain member can request
  reactivation with `previous_status: "inactive"` and apply the approved review
  without creating a second membership.
- Updated the Community Domain dashboard owner/admin access-request apply error
  handling so `community_domain_member_review_stale` becomes plain recovery
  copy: the person is already active, so refresh the reviewer queue before
  taking another action.
- Updated the Community Domain dashboard error parsing so backend structured
  errors still produce recovery guidance when the shared API wrapper serializes
  the backend `detail` object into `err.message`. This keeps duplicate/open
  access-request copy reachable for `community_domain_membership_request_pending`
  and stale-apply copy reachable for `community_domain_member_review_stale`.
- Tightened the Community Domain dashboard access-request panel filter so it
  shows only self-service membership access/reactivation reviews carrying the
  `previous_status` snapshot. Generic `domain_member.upsert` governance reviews
  no longer get mislabeled as people asking to enter the domain.
- Corrected the lazy Access Requests panel copy so it no longer says the panel
  is only pending reviews. It now covers both requests that still need a
  decision and approved-but-unapplied membership changes, and the empty state
  says there are no open access requests instead of no pending requests.
- Updated the Community Domain product contract audit to cage open-status
  duplicate detection, the approved-but-unapplied test assertion, the
  previous-membership payload snapshot, the stale-apply guard, inactive-member
  reactivation coverage, frontend structured-error parsing, self-service access
  request filtering, truthful access-request panel copy, and the frontend
  stale-apply recovery copy.

  - `GET /community-domains/{community_domain_id}/membership-requests/my`
  - `POST /community-domains/{community_domain_id}/action-reviews/{review_id}/apply`
  - `POST /community-domains/{community_domain_id}/action-reviews/{review_id}/revision`
  - `POST /community-domains/{community_domain_id}/action-reviews/{review_id}/cancel`
- Frontend:
  - `/app/community-domain`

  - `/app/community-domain/:communityDomainId`
  - `/app/community-domains/:communityDomainId`
  - `/app/community-domain/:communityDomainId/dashboard`
- Behavior changed only for duplicate/open self-service Community Domain
  membership requests and stale application of those requests when current
  membership status no longer matches the reviewed previous status, plus
  non-member revision of the requester's own self-service `needs_changes`
  membership request, stale/already-active rejection during that revision path,
  applicant withdrawal of their own pending or needs-changes membership request,
  self-service-only filtering of duplicate membership-request detection and the
  requester's own status endpoint, including approval-progress counts for
  multi-approval self-service requests, the denied-access panel's visible
  revision and withdrawal actions for the applicant's own open request, the
  recovery panel's preference for current leaf revision rows over superseded
  parents, its preference for open request rows over closed history, and the
  dashboard's display of self-service access/reactivation requests. The
  owner/admin
  reviewer queue now also follows the same pending-only rule and shows pending
  child revisions instead of `needs_changes` parents, and the access-request
  panel no longer silently hides actionable rows after the first three or hides
  multi-approval progress from the reviewer or requester. The parent route's
  post-click success copy is also count-aware when a review remains pending
  after the current reviewer decision. This change does not introduce a new
  membership-granting route, decide reviews, create notifications, change auth,
  change permissions, alter schemas, activate billing, verify authority, or
  deploy to Render.

Unabated truth:
- This is local-only after the prior push; it has not been committed, pushed, or
  deployed.
- It fixes one duplicate-intake window and one status-based stale-apply
  overwrite window for self-service membership-request reviews, plus one
  needs-changes revision dead end for non-member applicants and one stale
  child-review creation path after direct activation, plus one withdrawal dead
  end for pending and needs-changes self-service membership requests, plus one
  status-route classification leak where generic self-targeted governance
  reviews could be shown as applicant membership requests, plus one
  applicant-facing payload leak where requester status and duplicate-request
  errors could expose reviewer decision notes, reviewer identities, recusal
  count, full decision records, and governance policy identifiers. The same
  scoped response now applies to self-service applicant create, duplicate,
  revision, duplicate-revision, cancellation, and status responses, while full
  governance payloads remain available to the existing member/admin review
  surfaces. It also exposes the `needs_changes` applicant revision path in the
  denied-access UI instead of forcing users to infer it or withdraw and restart,
  and it keeps applicants on the latest child revision after a parent review has
  already been revised. Owner/admin reviewer queues now match that lineage by
  ignoring needs-changes parents and showing pending child revisions. It does not
  implement full Community Domain onboarding, invitation codes, bulk import,
  node placement, activation gates, notifications, authority verification, Trust
  Events, Trust Passport, or TrustSlip behavior.
- A first attempt at the stale guard was too broad because generic
  `domain_member.upsert` reviews without `previous_status` were treated as
  stale. The full backend suite caught this, and the guard is now opt-in only
  for payloads that explicitly include `previous_status`.
- The backend/API is confirmed live at `1e396bd` by the owner's Render dashboard
  paste and a live `/health` check, but it was not deployed through GitHub
  Actions because `RENDER_API_KEY` is missing. Future backend-impacting deploys
  still need that secret configured or a confirmed Render-side/manual deploy.
- Current local dirt also still includes untracked `docs/external_review/` and
  `screenshots/`, which were intentionally excluded from the prior publish batch.
